A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PE-GQNN for geographic prediction. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A.1–A.4 were included, with relocated material matched to v1.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, learning curves and predictive-distribution analyses on California Housing, Air Temperature and 3D Road, including Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on the same three datasets, including revised benchmark scores, training times, interval coverage and geographic prediction maps in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: v2 replaces the final ordinary fully connected layers with partially monotonic Lipschitz blocks and specifies probit-transformed quantile inputs, whereas v1 proposes logit inputs. This substantially changes the quantile predictor and its monotonicity constraints. Delayed quantile injection, neighbor-target inputs and the underlying pinball objective remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate California Housing price prediction, Air Temperature prediction and 3D Road altitude interpolation using the same represented datasets and task requirements. The new geographic maps analyze the existing California Housing test set.

E2.justification: The reported comparison set is substantially narrowed. v1's tau-only variant corresponds to v2's PE-GNN with SQR, but the tau-plus-Structure comparator disappears. Table 3 drops GCN/GAT comparisons on Air Temperature and 3D Road and retains GSAGE comparisons. GCN/GAT remain in California Housing, and SMACNP participation is unchanged.

E3.justification: Within the retained experimental design, v2 replaces MADECP's mean absolute calibration discrepancy with a sum of squared discrepancies and adds 95% predictive-interval coverage and training-time evaluation. Dataset splits and neighbor counts remain unchanged. SQR retains the earlier MPE/pinball formulation.

E4.justification: Removing the intermediate tau-plus-Structure ablation eliminates the staged separation of structural and neighbor-target contributions. v2 also replaces the ten-observation density illustration with a three-observation comparison against PE-GNN and adds geographic prediction maps in Appendix A.3. v1's explicit empirical check reporting no quantile crossings is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, benchmark error bars or significance tests. The new coverage column evaluates predictive intervals; it does not provide statistical uncertainty estimates for benchmark scores. The Monte Carlo calibration reference remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 contain revised scores and epoch counts, added timing and coverage results, and removed ablation/backbone entries. For example, PE-GQSAGE MSE changes from 0.0089 to 0.0088 on California Housing and from 0.0023 to 0.0033 on Air Temperature. These concern a revised model, not established same-setting gains. Calibration values also use a different metric.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds Gaussian and logistic special-case derivations and an explicit Lipschitz function-class condition, replacing v1's shared-parameter and final-layer argument about crossings. These are limited mathematical extensions rather than a new general proof framework. The Monte Carlo convergence argument is retained in Appendix A.1.

C1.justification: v2 expands the stated contribution to an explicitly monotonic quantile architecture and theoretical special cases, including its relationship to PE-GNN. v1 foregrounded three architectural modifications and relied largely on empirical evidence against crossings. The broad predictive-accuracy, uncertainty-quantification and computational-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 introduces substantive limitations concerning Lipschitz constraints and tail approximation, and explicitly acknowledges PE-GNN's better calibration on 3D Road. It also explains how quantile-input transformations determine distributional form and interprets the revised density plots through varying shapes and scales, extending v1's discussion of approximately symmetric predictions.

D1.justification: v2 discloses learning rate, dataset-specific batch sizes, detailed sinusoidal encoding formulas, and layer dimensions, activations, dropout and parameter counts in Appendices A.2/A.4. These substantially improve implementation documentation without establishing changes to previously unspecified settings. Conversely, v2 removes the explicit PE-GQNN source-code link present in v1; this does not establish that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tagasovska and Lopez-Paz (2019), attributing the SQR loss to that work, and Nolte et al. (2023) for monotonic networks. These refine attribution and position the new component within prior research; the broader related-work framing remains.

P1.justification: v2 extensively revises the abstract, background and portions of the methodological and experimental narrative. Contributions are reorganized into two groups, technical explanations and the Monte Carlo argument move into a structured appendix, and Conclusion becomes Discussion. These changes substantially reorganize the exposition.

P2.justification: The pipeline figure is updated for monotonic blocks, while the earlier quantile-network overview moves to Appendix A.1. Learning curves and distribution diagnostics are consolidated into a redesigned figure. v2 adds geographic maps and two architecture tables, restructures Tables 1–3, and adopts substantially denser page layout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves methodological clarity and reproducibility through explicit monotonic blocks and detailed architectures, adds timing and interval-coverage evidence, and acknowledges calibration and approximation limitations. These gains are tempered by the loss of staged ablations, reduced cross-backbone evidence and omission of the PE-GQNN code link. The added theory also contains CDF/PDF and lower-tail derivative-sign errors. Together, the changes support a limited net quality improvement.
